from.place: The proof's assertion that a coherent sheaf of generic rank r has leading Euler-characteristic coefficient r times that of the ample line bundle

title: Leading coefficient from generic rank
statement: Let K be a field, let Y be an integral proper K-scheme of dimension g, let M be an ample O_Y-module [def-sc-ample], and let E be a coherent O_Y-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Suppose there is a nonempty open U of Y and an isomorphism between the restriction of E to U and the free O_U-module of rank r. Then the numerical polynomial m \mapsto \chi(Y, E \otimes M^{\otimes m}) [def-pc-euler-characteristic] has m^g coefficient r times the m^g coefficient of the polynomial m \mapsto \chi(Y, M^{\otimes m}); equivalently, g! times its m^g coefficient is r times g! times the m^g coefficient for M.

source.place: Varieties, Section 33.44, intersection-number and pullback argument used in the proof of Lemma 33.45.11 (Tag 0BEX): for g=dim(Y), comparison of the m^g Hilbert coefficients by generic rank; formalized as AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.fwdDiff_iter_eulerChar_tensorObj_tensorPow

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-filtration-integral-subschemes] to E. Its successive quotients are (i_j)_*I_j for integral closed subschemes Z_j of Y and nonzero coherent ideals I_j of O_{Z_j}. At the generic point of Y, each quotient with Z_j = Y has rank one (a nonzero ideal of the function field) and each quotient with Z_j != Y vanishes; additivity of rank in the filtration therefore gives exactly r quotients with Z_j = Y. For each such quotient use 0 → I_j → O_Y → O_Y/I_j → 0, where O_Y/I_j is supported on a proper closed subset of Y. Tensoring with the invertible module M^{⊗ m} is exact, and by [lem-pc-euler-additive] Euler characteristics are additive in these short exact sequences. By [lem-sc-snapper-numerical-polynomial] (with r = 1 and L_1 = M), for every coherent F supported on a proper closed subset of the integral g-dimensional Y, hence of dimension at most g − 1, the map m \mapsto \chi(Y, F \otimes M^{\otimes m}) is a numerical polynomial of degree at most g − 1; this applies to each O_Y/I_j and each (i_j)_*I_j with Z_j != Y. Hence χ(Y, E ⊗ M^{⊗ m}) − r · χ(Y, M^{⊗ m}) is a numerical polynomial of degree at most g − 1.

proof.text: Adding the degree-at-most-(g−1) difference to r times the Hilbert polynomial shows that χ(Y, E ⊗ M^{⊗ m}) is a numerical polynomial of degree at most g and has m^g coefficient r times that of χ(Y, M^{⊗ m}).
